steps: Close both hands into A fists, thumbs tucked firmly against the side of the curled fingers.
Press the two fists together in front of your chest, with their palms facing each other.
Slide your dominant fist backward so it moves directly behind the stationary non-dominant fist.
Keep the non-dominant fist held steady in place as the reference point for the movement.
Hold a neutral expression and keep the palms facing each other from start to finish.
tip: It belongs to the WITH sign family - join the A hands, then let the movement point the direction: back reads as behind.

steps: Flatten both hands with fingers together and thumbs tucked, palms facing the ground.
Raise the flat hands to about waist height, keeping them low in front of your body.
Touch the fingertips of the two hands together in the center to form one level plane.
Sweep both hands smoothly outward to the sides, spreading them wide like laying a surface.
Follow the sweep with your eyes and keep a neutral face, letting the wide flat motion carry the meaning.
tip: Lifeprint notes this also means carpet - picture smoothing a flat sheet across a room.

steps: Extend the index finger of your dominant hand and curl the remaining fingers shut.
Hold your non-dominant forearm flat and level in front of you, palm angled slightly downward.
Set the dominant index fingertip against the inside of the wrist and drag it steadily up the forearm.
Stretch the drag into one extra-long continuous pull so the extended movement itself means longer.
Watch the moving finger and slow the motion down; a bigger unhurried stroke reads as greater length.
tip: ASL compares by stretching the movement - a normal pull signs long, an extended pull signs longer.

steps: Form the letter N by folding the middle finger of your dominant hand over the thumb.
Hold the N hand at chest height with the fingers pointing up and the palm facing left.
Drive the whole hand straight upward several inches in one firm vertical stroke.
Keep the wrist straight through the lift so the movement reads as clearly upward.
End the stroke near chin level with a neutral face; upward on a map is the north you are naming.
tip: Think of a wall map - north sits at the top, so the N hand climbs upward for northern.

steps: Shape your non-dominant hand into a firm O and hold it upright at chest height.
Spread the fingers of your dominant hand, then bend the middle finger sharply at its largest knuckle.
Poke the bent middle finger into the opening of the non-dominant O hand.
Pull the finger back out and immediately slap your open dominant palm down over the O opening.
Make both the poke and the slap quick and snappy, since the sudden snap sells the fizzy idea.
tip: This is pop as in soda pop - mime the quick burst of a bottle opening for a cleaner production.

steps: Pinch your dominant thumb and fingers loosely together, as if gripping a thin matchstick.
Hold your non-dominant hand flat before your chest with the palm facing sideways and fingers up.
Strike the dominant fingertips downward across the base palm, like scratching a match to light it.
For the noun form, make two very small quick strikes instead of one sweeping stroke.
For the verb form, use one single large strike and keep your expression focused.
tip: This is the matchstick sense; matching two things as a pair belongs to the combine sign family.

steps: Shape your dominant hand into an F, thumb and index touching as if pinching a tiny ring.
Hold your non-dominant hand up with the fingers extended so the ring finger is easy to see.
Slide the F handshape down along the non-dominant ring finger, setting the imaginary band onto it.
Pause briefly with the F handshape resting at the base of the finger to show the ring in place.
Keep the non-dominant hand still and your face neutral, letting the F handshape tell the jewelry story.
tip: The F hand itself looks like a ring - pinch an imaginary band and slide it onto the finger.

steps: Hold your non-dominant hand flat and open at chest height, fingers together and pointing forward.
Form an X handshape with your dominant hand by hooking the index finger over the thumb.
Move the dominant X hand firmly toward the open base palm until it makes contact.
Draw the X hand back toward your body slightly right after contact to complete the demand.
Keep your expression serious throughout; a firm face matches the weight of an obligation.
tip: It sits in the same family as NEED, with the X hand adding the force of something demanded.

steps: Form the letter A with both hands by closing each into a fist with the thumb beside the fingers.
Bring the two A fists together in front of your chest so they touch like a close pair.
Rock the joined hands forward and back together, about three inches in each direction.
Repeat the forward-back rock a second time so the pair moves as one steady unit.
Keep a warm relaxed expression, since the sign describes an ongoing romantic relationship.
tip: This is the GO-STEADY sign - it covers dating as a relationship, not one single date night.

steps: Hold your dominant hand in a loose open shape with the fingers relaxed and slightly spread.
Start the hand near your chest at mid-torso height, as if you are just inside a building.
Sweep the hand upward and outward in a rising arc toward the open space ahead of you.
Repeat the up-and-out sweep a second time with a quick beat to name the noun outdoors.
Aim your gaze toward the open space as you sign, since the eyes help mark the outside area.
tip: One big sweep says go out; doubling the movement names the place - outdoors.
